description: LMFDB modular-form-database query attempt to identify the QOU substrate M_iso motive by matching its Frobenius coefficients against weight-5 rational newforms (Path A from docs/audits/2026-05-02-m-iso-l-function-handoff.md).
verdict_detail: Sandbox egress proxy denies all connections to lmfdb.org with HTTP 403 at the TLS-inspection layer. WebFetch and curl probes both fail. Other hosts (api.github.com) reach successfully, confirming the block is host-specific to LMFDB. Lookup must be rerun from an environment with allowlisted egress to www.lmfdb.org.

target.motive: M_iso = T ↔ ³He isobaric asymmetry motive
target.hecke_field: Q (rational eigenform; all a_p ∈ Z verified in exact ring arithmetic)
target.candidate_conductors_note: Full enumeration of 2^a · 5^b for a ∈ {1..6}, b ∈ {0,1,2} (18 levels). Sorted ascending. Earlier draft of this witness (commit aa68402eb) listed only [10, 20, 40, 50, 80, 100, 160, 200, 250, 400] — Gemini PR #527 review (r3178029008) flagged that as inconsistent with the conductor form (missing all b=0 levels and the larger b ∈ {1, 2} levels; including 250 = 2 · 5^3 which violates b ≤ 2). This corrected list is the authoritative search space.

control_probes.interpretation: TLS handshake completes (cert from 'sandbox-egress-production TLS Inspection CA'); proxy returns 403 before request reaches LMFDB origin

method.raw_observation: All lmfdb.org subpaths and both lmfdb.org / beta.lmfdb.org hosts return HTTP 403 with 21-byte body, regardless of UA, protocol (http/https), or accept header. Egress proxy certificate identifies as 'Anthropic sandbox-egress-production TLS Inspection CA', confirming the 403 originates at the sandbox boundary, not at LMFDB.

next_actions.description: Rerun this lookup from a session where egress to lmfdb.org is permitted (host workstation with Claude Code CLI, or a CI job with explicit network policy). Programmatic API: GET https://www.lmfdb.org/api/mf_newforms/?weight=5&dim=1&level=N for N ∈ candidate_conductors (the full 2^a · 5^b set above); for each label fetch /api/mf_newforms/{label}/?qexpansion=true and read traces / a_p. The traces array is 0-indexed (traces[k] = a_{k+1}); the target a_p values are at 0-based indices (2, 6, 10, 12, 16, 18, 22) for primes (3, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23).

If LMFDB egress remains blocked, use Sage/Pari (`Newforms(N, k, names='a')`) on the same host. Both ship with sufficient newform databases through level 1000 weight 8 to cover the candidate-conductor list.

If no LMFDB match exists once the lookup runs, escalate to Path B (direct Hecke-operator T_p computation in QOU.Hecke + WedderburnDecomp; 2-3 weeks substantive Lean + Python) or Path C (recursive-ascent extension to A ≥ 4 atoms).
